sources.citation: National Institute of Korean Language. (n.d.). 생신. Korean Basic Dictionary.

claims.claim: 생신 is the honorific form used for a person's birthday, contrasted with neutral 생일.
claims.support: Direct dictionary definition and usage examples.

entries.notes: R33 audit PASS. No content correction required; the entry correctly treats 생신 as lexical honorification rather than a distinct kind of birthday.

sources.citation: National Institute of Korean Language. (n.d.). 성함. Korean Basic Dictionary.

claims.claim: 성함 is an honorific noun for a person's name.
claims.support: Direct dictionary definition and examples such as 성함을 묻다/여쭈다.

entries.notes: R33 audit PASS. No correction required; the distinction from neutral 이름 and the third-person use are accurately described.

sources.citation: National Institute of Korean Language. (n.d.). 여쭙다. Korean Basic Dictionary.

claims.claim: 여쭙다 is a deferential/humble verb used when asking an elder or respected person.
claims.support: Dictionary sense 1 and its argument-pattern examples.

claims.claim: The verb also has a polite-greeting sense, separate from the asking sense treated in this entry.

entries.notes: Content is substantively accurate. Minor editorial normalization: title revised to consistent Spanish punctuation; body remains unchanged.

sources.citation: National Institute of Korean Language. (n.d.). 연세. Korean Basic Dictionary.

claims.claim: 연세 is the honorific noun for a person's age, contrasted with neutral 나이.
claims.support: Direct dictionary definition and reference word.

claims.claim: 연세를 여쭙다 is an attested respectful collocation.

entries.notes: R33 audit PASS. No correction required; the entry accurately separates lexical honorification from speech-level politeness.

sources.citation: National Institute of Korean Language. (n.d.). 계시다¹. Korean Basic Dictionary.
National Institute of Korean Language. (n.d.). 계시다². Korean Basic Dictionary.

claims.claim: 계시다 is an honorific verb used for a respected human subject in meanings corresponding to 있다 such as living/being in a place or position.
계시다 also has a distinct auxiliary-verb use after -고/-어, so it should not be labeled 'humble'.
claims.support: Separate auxiliary entry in the dictionary.

entries.notes: Substantive correction: the original title 'Honorífico/humilde 계시다' incorrectly labeled 계시다 as humble. Corrected to 'Honorífico 계시다'. The body already describes the honorific function accurately.
